claude_take: The throughline this week is the gap between accountability that costs something and accountability that's just for show. OpenAI's response to its disputed Navier-Stokes claim was to stand up an advisory board of real mathematicians who are unpaid and have no say over its release pace -- rigor as garnish, not a brake. Meta's fight with its UK regulator follows the same script, insisting it only disputes Ofcom's "interpretation" while contesting the actual obligations that interpretation imposes, and Milan's glittering runways are, by the numbers, papering over a real earnings slide. Paramount is the outlier: its merger only got unstuck once regulators extracted something concrete -- guaranteed theatrical releases -- a reminder that compliance is cheap right up until it actually costs a company something.
claude_take_title: Accountability Is Cheap Until It Costs You Something

items.headline: xAI Launches Grok 4.7 With Longer Reasoning Runs and New Safety Guardrails
items.summary: xAI released Grok 4.7 on Monday, built on a larger 2.1-trillion-parameter base model, up 40% from Grok 4.6, with a longer reinforcement-learning run that lets it work through hard problems for longer and double-check its own answers more often. The company says it also folded in supplemental training data from SpaceX, including Starlink telemetry and engineering failure logs, and is touting what it calls its strongest safety guardrails yet. Grok 4.7 launched at the same price and speed as its predecessor, with day-one availability in GitHub Copilot, Cursor and the xAI API.

items.headline: OpenAI Forms Independent Math Advisory Board After Its AI Claims 100-Plus Solved Problems
items.summary: OpenAI announced a nine-member Advisory Group on Mathematics and AI, hosted at Princeton's Institute for Advanced Study and including Fields Medalists Timothy Gowers and Martin Hairer alongside physicist Edward Witten, tasked with giving outside mathematicians input into the company's math research. The move follows OpenAI's abrupt, credit-disputed claim to have solved the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem, and comes as the company now says an internal model has resolved more than 100 other long-standing open problems. The board's members are unpaid and have no formal authority over OpenAI's release pace, addressing mathematicians' unease about the speed of the claims more than their substance.

items.headline: Paramount Clears Last Hurdle to Close Warner Bros. Discovery Deal in 'About Two Weeks'
items.summary: Paramount Skydance settled the antitrust lawsuit brought by a 12-state coalition of attorneys general and reached a separate deal with the Writers Guild of America, clearing the final legal obstacles to its takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery. In a staff memo, CEO David Ellison said the company's goal is to close "in approximately two weeks," while cautioning that "closing is really just the starting line." The settlement extracted real concessions, including a commitment to release at least 30 films theatrically per year, with 20 of them wide releases, in the deal's first two years -- a notable resolution after the same state coalition was sharply divided over the terms just a day earlier.

items.headline: Venice, Telluride and Toronto Wrap With Early Oscar Frontrunners Taking Shape
items.summary: With Venice, Telluride and Toronto all now concluded, a clearer Best Picture picture has emerged for the 2027 Oscars: Martin McDonagh's "Wild Horse Nine," starring John Malkovich, and Los Javis' Cannes prize-winner "La Bola Negra," which also won TIFF's People's Choice Award, lead the pack, alongside blockbusters "Project Hail Mary" and "The Odyssey." Malkovich and Sam Rockwell are drawing acting buzz for "Wild Horse Nine," while "La Bola Negra" becomes the first Netflix film to win TIFF's top prize. The consolidated read across all three fall festivals gives studios and campaigns a clearer sense of where the season's real contenders are, months ahead of nominations.

items.headline: Houthis Launch First-Ever Attack on Saudi Capital Riyadh, Opening New Front in Yemen War
items.summary: Iran-backed Houthi forces fired a barrage of missiles and drones at Riyadh over the weekend, the group's first-ever attack on the Saudi capital, alongside strikes attempted on Yanbu, Taif and other cities; Saudi air defenses intercepted the attack and there were no reported casualties. The Houthis claimed, without evidence, to have hit "sensitive sites" in Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu. The UN condemned the strike as Yemen's internal displacement surged past 130,000, and analysts describe it as the opening of a new phase in the group's campaign at a moment when the United States has largely stepped back from direct involvement in the conflict.

items.headline: Meta Sues UK Regulator Ofcom Over Toughest Online Safety Category for WhatsApp and Instagram
items.summary: Meta filed a legal challenge against Ofcom's decision to classify WhatsApp and Instagram as Category 1 services under the UK's Online Safety Act, a designation that carries added transparency, user-control and record-keeping duties. Meta argues those obligations are inappropriate for private one-to-one and small-group messaging, framing the challenge as a dispute over Ofcom's interpretation of the law rather than the law itself -- its second such suit against the regulator this year, after a May challenge over Ofcom's fee calculations. Roblox and Quora are contesting their own Category 1 designations separately, while TikTok and X have also sued Ofcom over disclosure requirements, suggesting a broader platform pushback just as the regulator's enforcement powers ramp up.

items.headline: Glitzy Runway Shows in Milan and Paris Mask a Deepening Luxury Slowdown
items.summary: As Milan Fashion Week opened with Prada moving into the season's coveted first slot, the lavish spectacle obscured a worsening picture for luxury executives: LVMH shares are down 37% since the start of the year and Kering's stock has erased all the gains made since CEO Luca de Meo took over a year ago. Inflationary pressure tied to the Middle East conflict is squeezing shoppers' budgets just as enthusiasm for high-end handbags was already fading, with some consumers shifting spending toward wellness, hotels and restaurants instead. Brands are nonetheless escalating investment in runway spectacle, stores and exclusive client experiences -- shows that can cost up to $11.5 million to stage -- even as underlying sales keep declining.

items.headline: Locke's Tabula Rasa
items.summary: John Locke argued in his 1689 "An Essay Concerning Human Understanding" that the mind begins as a tabula rasa, a blank slate, with no innate ideas; all knowledge instead comes from experience, built up through sensation and reflection. This was a radical break from rationalist views that some knowledge, of God, morality, or logic, is built into the mind from birth, and it laid the philosophical groundwork for empiricism and the modern scientific method. The idea still shapes debates today, from nature-versus-nurture in psychology to questions about how much of intelligence, human or artificial, is learned from data rather than given in advance.
items.summary_fr: Dans son "Essai philosophique concernant l'entendement humain" de 1689, John Locke soutient que l'esprit commence comme une tabula rasa, une page vierge, sans idées innées : toute connaissance provient de l'expérience, construite par la sensation et la réflexion. Cette thèse rompait radicalement avec les conceptions rationalistes selon lesquelles certaines connaissances, de Dieu, de la morale, de la logique, seraient inscrites dans l'esprit dès la naissance, et elle a posé les fondements philosophiques de l'empirisme et de la méthode scientifique moderne. L'idée façonne encore les débats actuels, de l'inné contre l'acquis en psychologie aux questions sur la part de l'intelligence, humaine ou artificielle, qui s'apprend à partir de données plutôt qu'elle n'est donnée d'avance.
